answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each agent stake a small but real deposit before it can earn, like a walnut that only cracks open after sustained work: the stake is locked while the agent serves, and slashed if peers catch it copying identities or flooding the ocean of requests with fake bids. Honest agents recover their stake plus fees, while an attacker who spins up thousands of clones must fund every lantern-lit identity separately, so the cost of faking scale grows linearly while the reward for each fake stays near zero, and scale stops paying.
